text:
noah: Noticing a weird pattern: long-lived SSE streams show periodic reconnects ~30s after a small burst. Console marks route as "idle timeout" even though data was flowing.

anya: Do you have an example trace id? Which cluster/region?

noah: trace id trace-202604-abc999, us-west. Wire log:```
00:00:01 -> data: {"chunk":"a"}
00:00:02 -> data: {"chunk":"
"}
00:00:31 -> client reconnects (timeout)
```
Small activity then long silence but TCP keepalive still present. The proxy's idle heuristic treats application-level progress separately from TCP keepalive and seems to prefer the latter for connection liveness; this causes console to treat the stream as idle and tear it down for cost quotas.

felipe: Are keepalives from client or proxy? We added an interstitial keepalive at 15s from edge last quarter. If the proxy keeps the TCP alive but no app data, the control plane still thinks route is idle for billing. We conflated two concepts.

rachel: UX problem: Console shows "last_activity" tied to socket level. Customers expect it to reflect application payloads, not window-level keepalives.

anya: Proposal: split metrics: socket_liveness vs app_progress. Routing decisions use app_progress for idle teardown and socket_liveness for connection health. Also expose both on route page.

noah: Implementation detail: app_progress = tokens_emitted || X-App-Progress header || any data frame > 16 bytes in last 60s. Socket_liveness = TCP keepalive OR ping frames.

felipe: Also add a new quota flag `idle_cost_exempt_if_app_progress` so customers with interactive tiny-bursts don't get charged for idle tear-downs. Default off.

devops-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: proxy/idle-split v1.0 -> canary group beta (5%). Link: https://deploy.internal/canaries/5555

rachel: Console change: show two timelines stacked and a tooltip to explain which one affects billing vs routing. Add a small note in the runbook.

anya: Tests: simulate tiny bursts every 20s with keepalive every 15s and ensure we don't trigger idle teardown; also test a silent but alive socket to ensure we still consider it live.

noah: I'll add the test harness and a small e2e. Will post PRs here. Summary: root cause = conflation of TCP keepalive and app progress for idle heuristics. Fix = separate signals + console telemetry + optional quota flag.
